passages.title: The Old Entrance Still Shown on a School Map
sentences: A printed school map showed visitors entering through the east gate.
On Friday, Kota saw a new sign outside: “Visitors, use the south gate.”
Construction had closed the east gate, but several old maps were still beside the station.
Kota checked the date at the bottom of one map and saw a date from last year.
He kept the map because many roads were still correct.
He told the teacher, and they placed a bright correction sticker over the old entrance arrow.
The sticker directed visitors to the south gate until construction ended.
The school also put a new digital map online and marked the old printed copies clearly.
Kota learned that an old map sometimes needs one important current correction.
passages.fullTranslation: 印刷された学校地図では、来訪者は東門から入るようになっていました。金曜日、航太は外の新しい案内に「来訪者は南門を使ってください」と書かれているのを見ました。工事で東門は閉鎖されていましたが、駅のそばには古い地図がまだ何枚か置かれていました。航太が地図の下の日付を見ると、前年の日付だと分かりました。多くの道路はまだ正しかったため、その地図を残しました。先生に伝え、古い入口の矢印の上に目立つ訂正シールを貼りました。シールは工事終了まで来訪者を南門へ案内しました。学校は新しいデジタル地図も公開し、古い印刷版にははっきり印を付けました。航太は、古い地図には大切な最新の訂正が一つ必要なこともあると学びました。

slashRows.jp: 先生に伝え、古い入口の矢印の上に目立つ訂正シールを貼りました。

slashRows.en: The sticker directed visitors to the south gate until construction ended.

passages.title: An Eraser Returned inside the Wrong Pencil Case
sentences: Mika found a white eraser inside her pencil case after art class.
She already had her blue eraser, so the white one was not hers.
The white eraser had a small star cut into one corner and a faint letter K.
During art, four pencil cases were together on one table.
Mika did not decide from K alone because two students had K names.
She asked both students to describe the missing erasers before showing it.
Kei said his had a star cut made by his older sister, while Kumi said hers had a red cover.
Mika returned the eraser to Kei and checked her case for other mixed items.
She learned that asking for a detail first can confirm an owner fairly.
passages.fullTranslation: 美香は美術の授業後、自分の筆箱の中に白い消しゴムを見つけました。自分の青い消しゴムがあったため、白い方は自分の物ではありませんでした。白い消しゴムの角には小さな星形の切り込みと薄いKの文字がありました。美術の時間、四人分の筆箱が一つの机に置かれていました。Kの名前の生徒が二人いたため、文字だけでは決めませんでした。消しゴムを見せる前に、二人へなくした物の特徴を尋ねました。圭は姉が星形の切り込みを入れた物だと言い、久美は赤いカバー付きだと言いました。美香は消しゴムを圭へ返し、ほかの物も自分の筆箱に混ざっていないか確認しました。美香は、先に特徴を尋ねると公平に持ち主を確認できると学びました。

passages.title: The Weather Chart with One Blank Tuesday
sentences: The science class recorded the weather at eight every morning for two weeks.
They made a wall chart, and Tuesday of the second week was blank.
Monday was sunny and Wednesday cloudy, but neither proved Tuesday's weather.
Ryo checked the class notebook and found that the student on duty had been absent Tuesday.
The class did not fill the blank by copying a nearby day.
They looked for another school record from the same time.
The garden club had written 'light rain at 8:00' on its watering sheet that Tuesday.
The class added light rain to the chart and wrote 'garden club record' below the entry.
Ryo learned to fill a missing record with evidence, not a nearby-day guess.
passages.fullTranslation: 理科のクラスは二週間、毎朝八時に天気を記録しました。壁の表を作ると、二週目の火曜日だけ空白でした。月曜は晴れ、水曜は曇りでしたが、どちらも火曜の天気を証明しませんでした。亮がクラスノートを調べると、火曜日の係の生徒が欠席していたと分かりました。クラスは前後の日を写して空欄を埋めませんでした。同じ時刻の別の学校記録がないか調べました。園芸部はその火曜日の水やり表に「8時、小雨」と書いていました。クラスは表に小雨と加え、その下に「園芸部記録」と書きました。亮は、欠けた記録は前後の日の推測でなく証拠で補うと学びました。

passages.title: The Classroom Plant Leaning toward the Window
sentences: A small classroom plant stood on a shelf near the back wall.
After one week, its top leaves leaned strongly toward the window on the left.
Mina wondered whether the plant was simply falling because one side was heavier.
She checked the pot and found it stable, while the new stems were bending toward the light.
She did not cut the leaning stems or tie them straight immediately.
The class turned the pot halfway around and marked its new position.
Three days later, the newest leaves had begun turning back toward the window.
They continued turning the pot a little each week so different sides received light.
Mina learned that changing one condition and observing later can test an idea without damaging the plant.

passages.title: A Club Badge Box with Two Different Sizes
sentences: The tennis club received a box of new cloth badges for its uniforms.
The box held small and large badges together.
The order sheet showed eight small and twelve large badges for twenty members.
Yuki first planned to hand them out from the box, risking wrong sizes.
She checked the uniform list, which already recorded each member's badge size.
The club separated the badges into two trays and labeled them S and L.
They counted eight in the S tray and twelve in the L tray before distribution.
The members said their names one by one, and Yuki matched each name with the size on the list.
The club learned that sorting by recorded size prevents mix-ups.

passages.title: The Two Gloves That Did Not Make a Pair
sentences: After a cold morning, the lost-item box held two black gloves.
They looked similar from far away, so Taku put them together as one pair.
He picked them up and saw that both were left-hand gloves.
One had three gray lines at the wrist, while the other had a small red thread near the thumb.
Taku did not pair them just because their color matched.
He placed each glove separately and added a note about the place.
Later, one student described the gray lines and another described the red thread.
Each student received one glove and continued looking for its true partner.
Taku learned to check side and details before pairing similar lost items.
